marc: Hey team — planning a 6-month move to Singapore for family reasons starting Sept. Do I need to change homebase or can I stay on US payroll? Curious about WFH stipend, local social security equivalents (CPF?), and health coverage while abroad.

zoe (People Ops): Hi @marc — please fill the international-remote form. Short answers: payroll depends on tax residency and local rules; stipend is normally prorated; benefits may have limits overseas.

emma: For Singapore specifically: if you're physically present and working, it can create local payroll obligations. CPF is employer/employee social security for Singapore Citizens/PRs only, so likely not applicable if you're a US citizen on temporary stay. But local employer obligations can still apply depending on presence and contract.

ryan (Tax): We run a two-scenario analysis: (A) remain on US payroll with potential local filing; (B) cutover to local payroll. For a 6mo stay we often trigger employer registration review. Need exact dates and address.

marc: Dates: depart 2024-09-10, arrive 2024-09-11, return 2025-03-10. Staying with spouse who has PR. I'm not contracting locally, just doing Redwood work remotely.

ryan (Tax): Thanks. Please DM passport copy and Singapore address. We'll check double taxation treaty and whether 183-day rule or local statutory employer registration applies. Expect ~7 business days for final decision after intake.

zoe (People Ops): WFH stipend policy: full monthly stipend allowed for short-term remote. For a 6-month relocation we typically approve monthly stipend but require receipts for coworking; we may cap certain allowances. Stipend will be prorated if partial months apply.

people-ops-bot: quick-link: international-remote-form https://rwd.internal/people-ops/international-remote (automated)

emma: Health benefits: US medical plans may provide limited out-of-network coverage but often at higher cost. For extended Singapore stays you should consider short-term international health coverage; benefits team can share options. Also confirm evacuation coverage if relevant.

marc: If we cutover to local payroll, will 401(k) contributions stop? What happens to vesting?

zoe (People Ops): If cutover occurs, US payroll deductions (401k) typically stop. Equity continues to vest per plan but tax withholding on exercises may differ. We'll coordinate with Comp & Legal.

ryan (Tax): Note: even if you remain on US payroll, you may have local filing obligations and employer reporting requirements. There is also potential permanent establishment risk if multiple employees are in a jurisdiction doing client-facing work — keep that in mind.

marc: Understood. Any immediate docs I should send?

ryan (Tax): Passport copy, local address, expected work schedule/timezones, last US paystub. Also sign consent for data transfer.

zoe (People Ops): I'll start the intake and schedule a 30-min sync with payroll/tax for next Tue.

marc: Form submitted (ID 1725001111). Thanks all :pray:

people-ops-bot: Reminder: submit coworking receipts within 30 days for reimbursement. Policy: https://rwd.internal/people-ops/wfh-stipend-policy

zoe (People Ops): Looping in benefits to propose international medical options after tax decision.

marc: Appreciate the fast help!
